*Note: This post was generated by AI as a sample. Please replace it with your own writing.*

This site is plain Markdown rendered in the browser by tiny-markdown (see `index.html` and `styles.css`): no database, no admin panel, no build step to write a post — just a text file. `scripts/build-index.py` regenerates `index.md`, the list of posts visitors start from, so a new file appears there automatically.

## Create a new file

Create a new Markdown file at the repository root named with this format:

```
YYYY-MM-DD-your-post-title.md
```

For example: `2026-06-18-solarpunk-in-la.md`

## Add front matter

Every post starts with a front matter block at the top of the file:

```yaml
---
layout: post-no-feature
title: "Your Post Title"
date: 2026-06-18
description: "A short description of the post."
category: articles
---
```

- `layout: post-no-feature` — uses the clean, image-free layout
- `title` — the post title displayed on the page and in listings
- `date` — shown under the title (the `YYYY-MM-DD-` file-name prefix is also used to sort posts newest first)
- `description` — shown in the post listing as a summary
- `category: articles` — keeps the post appearing in the `/articles` index

`index.html` shows a note's `title` as an `<h1>` at the top, and its `date`, when present, as an `<h3>` directly underneath. Notes without those fields get no header.

## Write your content

Below the front matter, write in standard Markdown. Paragraphs, headings, links, and lists all work as expected.

## Wiki links (with friendly links)

Link between posts and pages in this repository with **wiki links** — the double-square-bracket syntax used by [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md), the note-taking app, whose [internal-links documentation](https://help.obsidian.md/Editing+and+formatting/Internal+links) this site follows. The renderer in `index.html` understands the same syntax and navigates to the target in-page, without a full page reload.

A wiki link names its target file without the `.md` extension; the renderer appends `.md` and loads that file:

```markdown
[[README]]
[[2026-06-21-westwood-greenway]]
```

On its own, that displays the target's file name. To show something people actually want to read instead, add a **friendly link**: display text after a pipe (`|`), in the form `[[target|Friendly display text]]`:

```markdown
[[2026-06-21-westwood-greenway|Visiting the Westwood Greenway]]
[[README|our README]]
```

(Write examples like these in a fenced code block, as above, so they are shown literally rather than turned into links.)

The first part is the target (the file name, minus `.md`); the second is the friendly text the visitor sees and clicks. This is the same form the generated `index.md` uses for every entry, for example [[2026-06-21-westwood-greenway|Visiting the Westwood Greenway]] — and you can use it the same way in a sentence, as in [[README|our README]].

A few conventions:

- Point a wiki link at a file that exists in the repository, relative to the repository root (a subfolder path works too).
- Keep titles and friendly text free of `|` and `]`, which would break the syntax.
- Use wiki links for links *within* this site. For links to other websites, standard Markdown still works: `[westwoodgreenway.org](https://westwoodgreenway.org)`.
- For images, video, and audio, use the embed form `![[ ]]` — the leading `!` makes it an embed rather than a link, and the text after the pipe is the alt/caption:

  ```markdown
  ![[charles_teaching.jpg|charles teaching]]
  ```

  Standard Markdown images and `<img>` tags are not used in this site, and the build fails if it finds one. See the "Images and other embeds" section of [[README|the README]].

## Publish

Commit the file and push to the `main` branch. The GitHub Actions workflow regenerates `index.md` and GitHub Pages rebuilds the site automatically within a minute or two — no other file needs editing.

- [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md) and its [help on internal (wiki) links](https://help.obsidian.md/Editing+and+formatting/Internal+links) — the syntax described above
- [Jekyll](https://jekyllrb.com) — the static site generator this site was originally built with, before moving to plain Markdown plus tiny-markdown
